nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime number, $e \ge 0$ an integer and $L$ a number field. Let $E_1$ and $F$ be subfields of $L$ such that $E_1$ is a $p^e$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and $F \subseteq E_1$. If $p$ is unramified in $F$, that is, every prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ lying over $p\mathbb{Z}$ is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$, then $F = \mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.title: Subfields of a $p$-power cyclotomic field unramified at $p$ are trivial

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ and $p$ be distinct prime numbers, and let $K$ be a number field that is an $\ell$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Then the quotient ring $\mathcal{O}_K / p\mathcal{O}_K$ is a field (that is, $p$ is inert in $K$) if and only if the multiplicative order of $p$ modulo $\ell$ is $\ell - 1$.
nodes.title: Inert primes in prime cyclotomic fields

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$, let $p$ be a prime number, and let $m'$ be $m$ divided by the largest power of $p$ dividing it, so that $m = p^a m'$ for some $a \ge 0$ with $p \nmid m'$. Then $p$ is unramified in the $m'$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{m'})$, where $\zeta_{m'}$ is a primitive $m'$-th root of unity: every prime ideal of its ring of integers lying over $p\mathbb{Z}$ is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: The $p$-free part of $m$ gives a cyclotomic field unramified at $p$

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $p$ be a prime number with $p \nmid m$. If $K$ is a number field that is an $m$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ (that is, $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ for a primitive $m$-th root of unity $\zeta_m$), then $p$ is unramified in $K$: every prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ lying over $p\mathbb{Z}$ is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Cyclotomic fields are unramified at primes not dividing $m$
